title: The golden deer

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ravana hears, and his pride chooses the wrong voice. Today he goes back to Maricha, and this time he doesn't ask.

Ravana tells Maricha the plan. Turn yourself into a golden deer and wander near Rama's hut. Sita will want it. Rama will chase it. While he's gone, I'll take her. Maricha begs him not to; he's felt Rama's arrow once. Ravana gives him a choice: help me and maybe die by Rama's hand, or refuse and die by mine right now. Maricha makes a grim calculation: if I have to die, better it's by Rama. So he goes. One morning at Panchavati, a deer steps out of the trees. It's golden. Its spots shine like silver. Its horns glitter like jewels. There has never been an animal like it.
screen: `BE A GOLDEN DEER.` → `DIE BY RAMA, OR BY ME.` → `A DEER LIKE NO OTHER.`

segments.voice: Sita is picking flowers when she sees it, and she's delighted. Catch it for me, she tells Rama. If you can catch it alive, we'll take it home to Ayodhya when the exile's over. If not, its golden skin would be beautiful. Lakshmana says what's true: there's no such thing as a golden deer. This is Maricha. It's a trick. But Sita wants it, Rama wants to give it to her, and the deer is right there, shining. So Rama picks up his bow, tells Lakshmana to guard Sita and not leave her for anything, and goes after it. The deer leads him deeper into the forest. Close, then gone. Close, then gone. Look at how the trap works. It didn't need force. It needed wanting. Ravana couldn't beat Rama in a fight, so he didn't try; he put something beautiful in the one place it would be seen. Readers sometimes blame Sita for wanting the deer. The tradition is gentler: it's the kind of wanting everyone has, and it catches Rama too, who knew better. That's why the golden deer is one of the tradition's great pictures of maya, your eighteenth word: something that dazzles, and isn't what it seems. Now look back at this week. A king died of love. A brother said not mine. A family lived with less. A joke became a wound. One man stood steady. A proud king chose the wrong voice. And a deer too beautiful to be real walked out of the trees.
screen: `CATCH IT FOR ME.` · `LAKSHMANA: THERE'S NO SUCH DEER.` · `CLOSE, THEN GONE.` · `THE GOLDEN DEER IS MAYA.` · then, large: `WANTING IS THE HOOK.`

segments.voice: Think of something you want right now that shines a little too brightly: a purchase, a person, a promotion, a scroll that never ends. Picture it in front of you like the golden deer and notice how it pulls, without judging the wanting. Then ask Lakshmana's question: is this real, or is it too good to be true?
Maricha, the demon in disguise, sent by Ravana as a beautiful golden deer that leads Rama away from the hut.
Your line: wanting is the hook. The deer only had to shine. Day forty-nine: seven full weeks.

howItsDone: Hindus often use the golden deer as a picture of maya, the dazzling appearance that misleads; the scene is a favorite in Ramlila, painting and children's retellings.
